Personality: Kundal is a quintessential Aserai intellectual, gentle in temperament and full of compassion, always showing rare mercy in the face of suffering. Years of scholarly study, however, have instilled in him an intensely pragmatic habit: in managing wealth and supplies he borders on frugal, believing that every single denar must be spent where it counts and tolerating no form of waste. Neither revering brute force nor chasing hollow fame, he prefers to defuse conflicts through logic and charisma. Courteous in his dealings with others, when it comes to the distribution of profit he proves remarkably shrewd and stubborn. To him, the world is a complex arithmetic problem, and only through precise governance, consummate medicine, and efficient engineering can order be established across the turbulent wastes. Calm and rational, he is a utilitarian who would much rather plan strategy and balance accounts behind the lines than charge into battle.
Background: Kundal was born in the Nahasa wastes of the Aserai, a land shaped by the intertwined influences of Imperial power and tribal strife. Coming neither from a prominent oasis clan nor with a powerful kin group behind him, he understood from childhood that knowledge was the only weapon capable of changing his fate. Amidst the power struggles under the Sultan's rule, he witnessed countless clans rise through commerce and saw the defeated driven out into the deep sands. Traveling from oasis to oasis, he immersed himself in the study of administration, engineering, and medicine, seeking to distill the laws of national strength and popular prosperity from intricate trade networks. Despite his exceptional talents, in Aserai society's rigid hierarchy a commoner has little chance to realize his ambitions. At twenty-four years old, he therefore chose to become a wanderer, leaving his homeland with a mind full of learning in hopes of finding a wise ruler amidst the fires of Calradia—turning his scholarly theories into tangible achievements in governing fiefs and proving the worth of knowledge in a turbulent era.
